---
title: "MixSIARPFN on every simulated dataset"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{MixSIARPFN on every simulated dataset}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2, out.width = "100%")
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
            theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
                  legend.position = "top"))
ss <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "simstudy.rds", package = "MixSIARPFN"))
bm <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "benchmark.rds", package = "MixSIARPFN"))
sc <- ss$scores
set_lab <- c(geese = "Geese-like", wolves = "Wolves-like, diets from the prior",
             wolves_realistic = "Realistic wolves-like")
err_col <- c(`Residual * Process` = "#D55E00", `Residual only` = "#0072B2",
             `Process only` = "#009E73")
pct <- function(x, d = 0) paste0(format(round(100 * x, d), nsmall = d), "%")

# Simulation study, per dataset
pd <- aggregate(cbind(crps, covered) ~ set + dataset + method, sc, mean)
w <- reshape(pd, idvar = c("set", "dataset"), timevar = "method", direction = "wide")
conv <- function(m) {
  x <- unique(sc[sc$method == m, c("set", "dataset", "converged")])
  stats::setNames(x$converged, paste(x$set, x$dataset))
}
w$conv_long <- conv("MixSIAR long")[paste(w$set, w$dataset)]
w$conv_normal <- conv("MixSIAR normal")[paste(w$set, w$dataset)]
n_ss <- nrow(w)

# Benchmark
d <- bm$designs
cm <- merge(bm$comparison, d[, c("dataset", "family", "error")])
diet <- cm[cm$quantity == "diet", ]
per_ds <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(diet, diet$dataset), function(x) data.frame(
  dataset = x$dataset[1], w1 = mean(x$wasserstein1, na.rm = TRUE),
  sd_ratio = stats::median(x$sd_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
  pfn_cov = mean(x$pfn_truth_in_95, na.rm = TRUE),
  mix_cov = mean(x$mixsiar_truth_in_95, na.rm = TRUE), n = nrow(x))))
d <- merge(d, per_ds)
n_bm <- nrow(d)
n_runs <- nrow(ss$mixsiar_seconds) + n_bm
```

Every simulated dataset made while developing MixSIARPFN that MixSIAR has also fitted
is here: `r n_ss + n_bm` datasets with known true diets, and more than
`r format(floor(n_runs / 100) * 100, big.mark = ",")` MixSIAR runs. They come in two groups:

- **The simulation study** (`r n_ss` datasets): three designs copied from MixSIAR's
  geese and wolves examples, 150 datasets each. The article *How MixSIARPFN works and
  how well it does* (`vignette("performance")`) analyses these in detail; this
  article gives the per-batch results.
- **The benchmark** (`r n_bm` datasets): designs chosen to cover what MixSIARPFN
  supports, from 2 to 8 sources, 1 to 4 tracers, 2 to 800 consumers, every error
  structure, fixed, random, crossed and nested effects, covariates, concentration
  dependence, sources given by a factor and informative priors.

MixSIARPFN fitted every one of them, each in about a second, with the released
(version 3) networks.

## The simulation study

```{r ss-table}
batch <- substr(w$dataset, 1, 1)
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(set_lab), function(s) do.call(rbind, lapply(c("a", "b"), function(b) {
  x <- w[w$set == s & batch == b, ]
  ok <- x[x$conv_long, ]
  data.frame(set = set_lab[[s]], batch = c(a = "1 (seed 2026)", b = "2 (seed 2027)")[[b]],
             n = nrow(x), long_conv = sum(x$conv_long), normal_conv = sum(x$conv_normal),
             crps_pfn = mean(ok$`crps.MixSIARPFN v3`), crps_mix = mean(ok$`crps.MixSIAR long`),
             better = sum(ok$`crps.MixSIARPFN v3` < ok$`crps.MixSIAR long`),
             cov_pfn = mean(x$`covered.MixSIARPFN v3`), cov_mix = mean(ok$`covered.MixSIAR long`))
}))))
knitr::kable(tab, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 4, 4, 0, 3, 3), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Design", "Batch", "Datasets", "MixSIAR long converged",
                           "MixSIAR normal converged", "CRPS, MixSIARPFN", "CRPS, MixSIAR long",
                           "MixSIARPFN more accurate", "95% coverage, MixSIARPFN",
                           "95% coverage, MixSIAR long"),
             caption = "CRPS and 'more accurate' are over the datasets where MixSIAR's long run converged; MixSIARPFN's coverage is over all datasets.")
```

The two batches were simulated separately, with different random seeds, and they tell
the same story: MixSIARPFN's accuracy is close to converged
MixSIAR's in every batch, it is the more accurate on about a third of datasets, and
its intervals cover the truth at least as often as they should. Against MixSIAR's
normal-length run, which most analyses use, it is the more accurate on
`r sum(w$"crps.MixSIARPFN v3" < w$"crps.MixSIAR normal")` of all `r n_ss` datasets,
including the `r sum(!w$conv_normal)` where that run had not converged.

## The benchmark

```{r bm-table}
dt <- d[order(d$family, d$error, d$sources), ]
dt$design <- paste0(dt$effects, ifelse(dt$covariate, " + covariate", ""),
                    ifelse(dt$conc_dep, ", conc.", ""), ifelse(dt$sources_by_factor, ", sources by factor", ""),
                    ifelse(dt$informative_prior, ", informative prior", ""))
dt$name <- sub("^[a-z]+/(ov[0-9]+).*$", "\\1", dt$dataset)
dt$mixsiar <- paste0(dt$mixsiar_run, ifelse(dt$mixsiar_psrf > 1.1, " (not converged)", ""))
knitr::kable(dt[, c("family", "name", "error", "sources", "tracers", "consumers", "design",
                    "mixsiar", "n", "w1", "sd_ratio", "pfn_cov", "mix_cov")],
             digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 2, 2, 2), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Family", "Dataset", "Error", "Sources", "Tracers", "Consumers",
                           "Effects and options", "MixSIAR run", "Diets compared",
                           "Mean W1", "Median SD ratio", "Coverage, MixSIARPFN",
                           "Coverage, MixSIAR"))
```

For every diet proportion of every dataset (global, each level, along a covariate and
combinations of levels), MixSIARPFN's posterior is compared with MixSIAR's draws:

- **W1** (Wasserstein-1): how far, on average, probability has to move to turn one
  posterior into the other, in units of the proportion. 0.02 means the two posteriors
  are typically 0.02 apart.
- **SD ratio**: MixSIARPFN's posterior SD over MixSIAR's (above 1: MixSIARPFN is wider).
- **Coverage**: how often each method's 95% interval contains the true value.

Across all `r n_bm` datasets the mean W1 is `r round(mean(diet$wasserstein1, na.rm = TRUE), 3)`,
the median SD ratio `r round(stats::median(diet$sd_ratio, na.rm = TRUE), 2)`, and the 95%
coverage `r pct(mean(diet$pfn_truth_in_95, na.rm = TRUE))` for MixSIARPFN against
`r pct(mean(diet$mixsiar_truth_in_95, na.rm = TRUE))` for MixSIAR.

### The two methods give the same diets

```{r means, fig.height = 3.6}
ggplot(diet, aes(mixsiar_mean, pfn_mean, colour = error)) +
  geom_abline(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = err_col, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ error) + coord_equal() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  labs(x = "MixSIAR posterior mean", y = "MixSIARPFN posterior mean")
```

Each point is one diet proportion in one dataset (`r nrow(diet)` in all). The two
methods' posterior means agree closely across every design and error structure: the
correlation is `r round(stats::cor(diet$pfn_mean, diet$mixsiar_mean), 3)`, and half
of them differ by less than
`r round(stats::median(abs(diet$pfn_mean - diet$mixsiar_mean)), 3)`.

### Dataset by dataset

```{r w1, fig.height = 5.5}
dd <- d
dd$name <- paste0(sub("-like", "", dd$family), " ", sub("^[a-z]+/(ov[0-9]+).*$", "\\1", dd$dataset))
dd$name <- stats::reorder(dd$name, dd$w1)
ggplot(dd, aes(w1, name, colour = error, shape = mixsiar_psrf > 1.1)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = err_col, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 1), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Mean W1 between MixSIARPFN's and MixSIAR's diet posteriors", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

```{r w1-top, include = FALSE}
top <- d[order(-d$w1), ][1:3, ]
top_txt <- paste0(sub("-like", "-like", top$family), " ", sub("^[a-z]+/(ov[0-9]+).*$", "\\1", top$dataset),
                  " (", top$effects, ", ", top$sources, " sources; W1 ", round(top$w1, 3), ")")
```

`r sum(d$w1 < 0.03)` of the `r n_bm` datasets sit below 0.03: there the two posteriors
are nearly the same. The largest differences are `r knitr::combine_words(top_txt)`.
Open circles are the two datasets where MixSIAR itself had not fully converged
(largest PSRF 1.29, both with a covariate); the two methods agree closely even there.

### Calibration

```{r coverage}
cv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(diet, diet$error), function(x) data.frame(
  error = x$error[1], datasets = length(unique(x$dataset)), diets = nrow(x),
  pfn = mean(x$pfn_truth_in_95, na.rm = TRUE), mix = mean(x$mixsiar_truth_in_95, na.rm = TRUE))))
knitr::kable(cv, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 3, 3), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Error structure", "Datasets", "Diet proportions",
                           "95% coverage, MixSIARPFN", "95% coverage, MixSIAR"))
```

### Model parameters

```{r params}
pr <- cm[cm$quantity != "diet", ]
pr$what <- c(sd = "Random-effect SDs", resid = "Residual multipliers (resid.prop)",
             slope = "Covariate slopes (CLR)")[pr$kind]
pt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(pr, pr$what), function(x) data.frame(
  what = x$what[1], n = nrow(x), datasets = length(unique(x$dataset)),
  cor = stats::cor(x$pfn_mean, x$mixsiar_mean),
  sd_ratio = stats::median(x$sd_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
  pfn = mean(x$pfn_truth_in_95, na.rm = TRUE), mix = mean(x$mixsiar_truth_in_95, na.rm = TRUE))))
knitr::kable(pt, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 3, 2, 2, 2), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Parameter", "Estimates", "Datasets", "Correlation of means",
                           "Median SD ratio", "Coverage, MixSIARPFN", "Coverage, MixSIAR"))
```

MixSIARPFN also gives the model's other parameters, and they agree with MixSIAR's as
closely as the diets do. Random-effect SDs are hard for both methods: they are weakly
identified with few levels, and both methods' intervals miss the true SD more often
than 5% of the time.

## Datasets left out

```{r excluded}
knitr::kable(bm$excluded, col.names = c("Dataset", "Why it is not compared"))
```

These are cases where there is no reliable MixSIAR answer to compare with.

## In short

Across `r n_ss + n_bm` simulated datasets and every kind of model MixSIARPFN supports,
its posteriors are close to MixSIAR's and its intervals are calibrated. In the
simulation study, where accuracy against the truth can be compared directly, it is the
more accurate of the two on about a third of datasets. And it takes about a second
where MixSIAR takes from minutes to hours.
